question.text: In an experiment with vernier callipers of least count <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, when two jaws are joined together the zero of vernier scale lies right to the zero of the main scale and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>6</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of vernier scale coincides with the main scale division. While measuring the diameter of a spherical bob, the zero of vernier scale lies in between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> marks and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> division of vernier scale coincides with the main scale division. The diameter of bob is measured as

solution.text:
The least count is LC=0.1 mm

Zero error (ZE)=6×LC=6×0.1 mm=0.6 mm

The total reading is TR=MSR+VSR×LC-ZE⇒TR=32 mm+(0.1×4) mm-0.6 mm⇒TR=31.8 mm=3.18 cm
